'''Pliny Earle Chase''' (August 18, 1820, in [[Worcester, Massachusetts]] &ndash; December 17, 1886, in [[Haverford, Pennsylvania]]) was an American [[scientist]], [[mathematician]], and [[educator]] who contributed to the fields of [[astronomy]], [[electromagnetism]], and [[cryptography]], among others.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Garrett, Philip C.|title=Memoir of Pliny Earle Chase|journal=Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society|date=July–December 1887|volume=24|issue=126|pages=287–295|jstor=983078}}</ref>

==Biography==
He graduated at [[Harvard University|Harvard]] in 1839, then taught in [[Philadelphia]] and engaged in business for many years, but employed his leisure in physical and philological studies. In 1863, he was elected a member of the [[American Antiquarian Society]] and the [[American Philosophical Society]].<ref>[http://www.americanantiquarian.org/memberlistc American Antiquarian Society Members Directory]</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Pliny Chase |url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=chase%2C+pliny&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced |website=American Philosophical Society Member History Database |access-date=16 February 2021}}</ref> In 1864, the [[Magellanic Premium|Magellanic gold medal]] of the [[American Philosophical Society]] was awarded him for his ''Numerical Relations of Gravity and Magnetism''. The results of other mathematical and physical researches were published from time to time in the ''Proceedings'' of the American Philosophical Society, and brought him a worldwide reputation as a man of unusual scientific powers and attainments. In 1871, he became a member of the faculty of [[Haverford College]], [[Pennsylvania]], and for a long time was professor of philosophy and logic.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Death of Pliny E. Chase|journal=Friends' Intelligencer United with the Friends' Journal|year=1886|volume=43|pages=826–827|location=Philadelphia|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=c-MpAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA826}}</ref> He published ''Elements of Meteorology'' (1884).

==Family==
His brother [[Thomas Chase (educator)|Thomas Chase]] was a noted Latin scholar. His mother, Lydia Earle Chase, was the daughter of the famous inventor [[Pliny Earle I|Pliny Earle]]. Pliny Chase had two brothers and three sisters. His sister [[Lucy Chase]] (1822–1909) was a noted [[abolitionist]], supporter of [[women's suffrage]] and the [[temperance movement]], and teacher in contraband camps and freedman schools in the American South.<ref>[http://www.lexisnexis.com/documents/academic/upa_cis/10853_newenglwomfamserapt3.pdf Chase Family Papers], c. 1787–1915.</ref> Upon his death, Pliny Chase left a widow, two sons and three daughters.<ref>Samuel S. Green, [https://books.google.com/books?id=EHIPAAAAYAAJ "Pliny Earle Chase"], ''Proceedings of the American Antiquarian Society'', Volume 4, April 1887, p. 319.</ref>
